market_holds: Spot 47.78 (sealed 18:10 UTC). The stock is down 38.6% over 20 sessions and 11.1% over 5, 65% below its 52-week high and 9% above its low (sealed baseline). Front-week straddle 18.2%, event-implied move 16.1%. Put skew is 14.3 vol points (25d put IV minus 25d call IV), so downside protection is expensive. Press quotes of the implied move run 18-21% (TipRanks 2026-11-07, OptionSlam). The last four prints moved +19.3, -11.4, -18.5 and -16.3 (median absolute 17.4%, 1 of 4 up). Consensus Q3: revenue $3.54B, slightly above the $3.45-3.60B guide midpoint and up from about $3.30B when the guide was given. Non-GAAP EPS consensus is -1.17 to -1.27 with a whisper of -1.00 (Finviz/Earnings Whispers 2026-11-03, TipRanks 2026-11-07). Q4 consensus is about $4.69B (Benzinga snapshot), which puts FY consensus near $12.9B against the $12.4-13.2B guide (own arithmetic). Implied Q4 at the guide midpoint is about $4.62B, a step-up of roughly 31% on Q3. Guide from 2026-08-11: Q3 adjusted operating income $200-260M, Q3 interest expense $860-940M, Q3 capex $11.5-13.5B, FY capex $35-39B, active power above 1.85 GW at year-end (1.5 GW at Q2), low-teens adjusted operating margin in Q4, exit ARR $18.5-19.5B, and above 3 GW active by end-2027. The stock trades on financing and credit more than on the quarter. The 5-year CDS hit a record of about 1,000-1,195bp in mid-October and the 9.625% 2032 notes went below 80 cents. There was a $4.2B 2.875% convertible on 2026-09-22 and a 35M-share ATM on 2026-09-17. Peers sold off with it: from Oct 6, IREN fell 40% and NBIS 36%. On 2026-11-05 the stock fell 9% after Microsoft walked away from a Nscale Texas expansion. Short interest was 69.8M shares on 2026-10-15, up from 59.95M on 9/30 and 54.9M on 9/15, at 1.7 days to cover. Part of that rise is probably convertible-arb hedging. Sell-side: 21 Buy, 5 Hold, 3 Sell. Previews cut targets but kept ratings (Citi $128 on 2026-11-04, UBS $105).
view: This print is a credit-stress equity reporting a quarter whose operations are probably fine. The counterparties' own disclosures say Q3 capacity landed. Applied Digital reached ready-for-service on a second 75 MW at Polaris Forge on 2026-10-01, for 250 MW live, against 175 MW on Jul 1. Core Scientific went from billing 437 MW in mid-July to 485 MW at its 2026-11-05 report, with 100 MW more commissioning and the Dalton Phase 2 timing unchanged. Galaxy had delivered Helios Phase I in full. Pricing went up about 25% in July, and more than $25B of Q3 commitments were already disclosed on the August call, so the backlog headline should step up from $104B. A revenue beat and a bigger backlog are therefore likely. But consensus has already climbed above the guide midpoint, so that part is largely in the number. The reaction will turn on three things this release reveals and that I cannot see in advance. (1) The Q4 and full-year guide against a back-end-loaded $4.69B Q4 consensus. That Q4 needs roughly 350 MW more active power in H2, at a time when the industry is paying penalties of more than $5M a day for late capacity (The Information via TIKR, 2026-10-26). The same set-up a year ago (Nov 2025) produced a delay-driven guide cut and -16%. (2) The first framework for 2027 capex and how it is funded, given the above-3 GW target for end-2027. A huge number in this tape is a negative. A slower build that protects credit cuts both ways. (3) Interest expense near $900M against about $230M of adjusted operating income, plus how much of the ATM was used. The prints on Feb 26, May 7 and Aug 11 all moved with how the next-period guide stood against consensus. Positioning cuts both ways. A 40% slide in a month, rising short interest and rich puts give an in-line print plus a clean guide room for a sharp relief rally, as in August (+19%). Any new financing or delay wrinkle lands on a market that already prices distress, and the last three of four prints fell. Nebius reports before the open on 2026-11-11, inside this window, which adds a peer read I cannot sign. I find no dated evidence the price misses in a knowable direction, so this is a near coin flip with a slight downward lean from the base rate and the back-loaded Q4.

recommendation.reason: The operating evidence I can find from counterparties (APLD, CORZ, Galaxy) points to Q3 capacity on schedule. But consensus already sits above the guide midpoint, so that is held. The reaction will be decided by the Q4 guide against a back-loaded $4.69B consensus, the 2027 capex and financing framework, and the interest burden. None of these has a public trace I can sign before the release, so there is no mechanism to recommend on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Holding or raising the FY2026 revenue guide and the above-1.85 GW year-end power target, together with a 2027 capex plan that comes with named committed financing (prepayments or DDTLs), would make the relief rally the likely outcome. A cut to the FY guide or the power target for site delays would make the downside the likely outcome.

self_critique: The case for long is real. The stock is down about 40% in a month on credit fear rather than company data. Counterparty disclosures show capacity on schedule. Pricing rose about 25% in July. The backlog headline will jump. Rising short interest and expensive puts set up exactly the squeeze August produced (+19%). If management simply holds the FY guide and names committed 2027 financing, a 15-20% rally is plausible, and my 47 may be too bearish. The case for short is also real. Q4 is back-loaded against a consensus above the midpoint, industry delay penalties are rising, and a large 2027 capex framework could re-ignite the credit fear. Because the two cases balance and neither has a dated trace I can sign, I stay near 50.
approach_notes: Rebuilding the capacity line from counterparties' own filings (P3, 'stakeholders') was the most informative route and quickly showed the revenue line is held by consensus (P4). The playbook offers no route to the credit and financing narrative, which is what this stock trades on now, so the loop stopped early, as P8 says it should.
